spec.name: v4_funding_carry
spec.rationale: Hyperliquid perps settle funding every hour; a positive rate means longs pay shorts. Persistently high funding marks a crowded, leveraged long side that pays to stay in; the other side is paid to supply that exposure. Funding is persistent hour to hour, so the trailing rate forecasts the next day's payment. The known risk is the price leg: crowded longs are often in coins that keep rising (momentum), and squeezes hit shorts hardest. Dollar neutrality removes the market direction, not the coin-specific moves.

result.universe_rule: Every main-dex perp in the metadata at fetch time (listed or delisted), ranked by dollar volume (sum of hourly volume x close) over the formation window; the top 30 with at least 90% of formation hours present form the universe for the whole window. Builder (HIP-3) dexes excluded.

result.note: Design choice 1 of 2: rebalance weekly (every 168 h from the window start) instead of daily. Reason: in-sample costs ($209.51) exceeded the funding earned ($136.00) at 0.52x gross turnover per day; funding ranks persist for days, so a slower rebalance should keep most of the funding at a fraction of the cost. Rule fixed before this run: adopt it for the sealed run only if in-sample net P&L beats -$820.98; otherwise revert to the pre-registered daily config.
